#2154. 8 Windows apps you should probably remove from your PC

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1379 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

8 Windows apps you should probably remove from your PC

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1379 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Not every app on your PC deserves a permanent place.
  • Recent findings suggest that bloatware and adware aren't upcoming, but they feel far more prevalent these days.
  • The ubiquity of these annoyances, including junk built into Windows itself, means that debloating a fresh Windows PC has become a common practice.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Not every app on your PC deserves a permanent place.

Recent findings suggest that bloatware and adware aren't upcoming, but they feel far more prevalent these days. Not only do they take up SSD space (which is more precious than ever because of soaring storage prices), but they can also consume RAM and annoy you with alerts you don't care about.

The ubiquity of these annoyances, including junk built into Windows itself, means that debloating a fresh Windows PC has become a common practice. Some apps (both preinstalled and common third-party tools), aren't actively detrimental. But, depending on how you use your PC, it may be worth upgrading them with superior — and often inexpensive or free — options. Here are several such Windows apps you should replace or remove outright.

Industry observers note that media Player, not to be confused with the classic Windows Media Player from prior Windows versions, is the out-of-the-box way to listen to music or watch videos on your PC. And while it does a suitable job of playing both audio and video files from a broad range of formats, it can't compete with the features you get from alternative apps like VLC.

Recent findings suggest that VLC can play tons of video formats (even rare ones) without the need for additional codecs or extensions. It can also handle media file conversions rapidly and easily. If you love subtitles but have a video file that lacks them, VLC can take dragged-and-dropped .srt or .vtt files from the web. The totally-free app can do so much more once you dig into it.

It's never been easier to get into content creation, which can blossom into a potentially profitable side hustle. Even if not, it's fun sharing your creativity with close friends and anyone the algorithm pushes you towards. Microsoft Clipchamp is included in Windows 11 and offers a user-friendly way to crop, cut and edit videos in up to 1080p. Unfortunately, it keeps a lot of its flashier features, like Copilot integration and 4K exporting, along with access to premium stock assets, filters and effects, behind the Microsoft 365 paywall.

As someone who edits video almost every day, it's difficult for me to recommend anything else but CapCut to amateur creators. It's approachable for beginners while also providing plenty of features that professionals will love. And as someone leery about shoehorned AI features, I find those in CapCut actually useful (some of them, anyway).

There's a subscription here too if you want to take full advantage, starting at $19.99 per month. But it's one of the few apps on this payment model that provides substantial value.

Industry observers note that while it might sound shallow to say, uTorrent is one of the most hideous-looking modern apps. Like many programs that offer free versions, it's full of ads and foists extra junk apps on you during installation. In 2015, uTorrent received backlash after it secretly installed Epic Scale, a Litecoin miner, with every new installation. We're more than a decade removed from this, but it's the kind of cynical action that people never really forget.

It has been revealed that there are countless replacements, with two highlights depending on what you're after. For a uTorrent-like experience without the bloat or ads, there's qBittorrent. It's got a slightly larger footprint than uTorrent, has built-in search engines, and is widely accepted on private trackers. If you prefer a slimmed-down, barebones approach, Transmission is hard to beat.

Setting up a upcoming PC is exciting, but also comes with some frustrations. You'll probably be dismayed to see, after dropping major bucks on a new piece of tech, that you still have to contend with pre-installed software like Norton or McAfee. It's annoying to get bombarded with alerts that your trial (which you never wanted) is ending, especially since Windows Defender is more than enough for most people.

Considering how good Defender is, McAfee, Norton, and other antivirus apps don't simply provide protection from viruses. Their paid versions add other security services such as a VPN, scam detection and support for restoring your identity if it's stolen. But if you're just looking for bog-standard protection from viruses, Defender should be vigilant enough to keep your PC safe.

It has been revealed that does anyone actually use these? Despite their default presence in the world's most popular desktop OS, I've never once heard of anyone actually implementing the built-in news and weather apps in their regular workflow. It's almost impressive that Microsoft still supports these, which probably see less regular use than Minesweeper.

According to recent reports, the Weather app isn't terrible, but there's nothing particularly exciting about it and it also has annoying ads to work around. Plenty of weather sites give you more data in a cleaner experience. The News app is considerably worse, cramming tons of low-quality and clickbait stories amongst more ads. You'll have far better results curating a feed with RSS, following your favorite news publications on social media or getting alerts from their dedicated apps.

Sources indicate that while Xbox still has dedicated consoles, Microsoft's dedicated gaming brand has taken on a more nebulous definition. It's a console, but also an app and a store, with games you can stream to many other devices. If you're a gamer, the Xbox app for Windows has plenty of features and tools like Xbox mode that come close to providing a console-like experience with the power of your PC. It's constantly updated, supports cloud gaming, lets you easily connect with friends and aggregates all your games from various storefronts in one convenient place.

But if you're not a gamer, it does little more than take up resources. Even if you are a gamer, those who stick to Steam for their games can get by without the Xbox app. That's also the case for anyone who's hopped off the Game Pass bandwagon recently.

If you want a simple example of how cynical adware has gotten in recent years, just remind yourself that in the not-too-distant past, Minesweeper and Solitaire came standard with every copy of Windows and weren't bogged down with ads like they are today. You can pay for the premium edition of Microsoft Solitaire Collection for $1.49 per month, which won't break the bank, but still feels unnecessarily rent-seeking.

Sources indicate that but with games as simple as these, there are, luckily, many free alternatives easily accessible from your web browser. Solitaire for Free and Minesweeper for Free are exactly what they're poised as: classic versions of these games with no nonsense. Minesweeper doesn't offer much customization outside of difficulty, but Solitaire has more than 30 variations, plus light customization of its cards and background.

If you want an alternative that you can play offline, Free Solitaire on Steam is tough to beat. There are tons of different game modes and variants, lots of card customization (including personalized art if you want) and zero ads.

Sources indicate that one of the irrefutable facts of life is that "nothing beats free." Sure, there are outliers, but if I had to cite my source for this ancient adage, it would be Google Docs and the rest of Google Workspace. Google's productivity suite features everything most people need for personal documents, spreadsheets and presentations. And web links make them easy to share with whoever needs them.

It's not a one-to-one match for Microsoft Office, which is why many professionals still need the full Microsoft suite. Microsoft Office extensions like .docx and .xlsx are the corporate standard, and while Google Docs can export to these, doing so can result in some wonky formatting.

Unfortunately, accessing Microsoft Office applications requires paying at least $9.99 per month or $99.99 per year for Microsoft 365. If you prefer the feel of a dedicated app, or are leery of letting Google take over another part of your life, there are plenty of great Microsoft Office alternatives. One is OnlyOffice, which provides a comparable Office experience while also being free (with paid options for businesses and developers).

No matter which option you choose, you can uninstall the free Microsoft Office trials that come with Windows and only serve to push you into signing up for a subscription when you open an Office file.

Whatever the case, hopefully Motorola will speed things up over the next few years, especially with its $1,600 flagship Signature 27 on the horizon with the same software promises.

#2151. Should you go with a headphone DAC/amp combo or a stack?

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (631 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Should you go with a headphone DAC/amp combo or a stack?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (631 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Both will do a fine job, and it depends on what you need from your gear.
  • Sources indicate that you don't always need a DAC and amp to enjoy music through headphones.
  • In a recent development, A DAC and a headphone amp can come together in a single unit (usually known as a DAC/amp) or as a stack of separate units.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Both will do a fine job, and it depends on what you need from your gear.

Sources indicate that you don't always need a DAC and amp to enjoy music through headphones. If your computer or laptop's headphone jack already delivers clean audio at a comfortable volume, then you're probably fine. Some MacBooks from 2021 and later, for example, support both low- and high-impedance headphones and can deliver up to 3 volts RMS through their headphone jacks when you use headphones rated between 150 and 1,000 ohms. If your headphone jack isn't quite as capable, or if you're not satisfied with the sound, though, then it's time to spend on some hardware.

In a recent development, A DAC and a headphone amp can come together in a single unit (usually known as a DAC/amp) or as a stack of separate units. And while the latter seems like the more serious setup, it doesn't necessarily mean you'll enjoy a better listening experience. The main job of a DAC is to turn digital audio signals into analog signals, while the amplifier takes those analog signals and makes them loud enough to power your headphones. Both a DAC/amp combo and a stack do the same thing, and which you go for largely depends on your headphones, how much flexibility you need and, of course, your budget.

It has been revealed that for most listeners, a DAC/amp is the way to go, especially if you're trying to improve your computer's audio without taking up too much space. Not only is a single unit more convenient, but it also means fewer cables dangling around and one less power adapter to worry about. You can even use a portable USB-C DAC/amp dongle designed for smartphones, but desktop versions usually offer better connectivity and power.

Sources indicate that DAC/amps can also offer better value than separates, too. Schiit's Magni 6 sells for $169 with its optional internal USB DAC. Conversely, you can buy the Magni 6 sans DAC for $99 and pair it with the Modi 5 DAC for $149 (or $164 with a power adapter). That brings the total to over $250, and you don't even get an interconnect cable. The Modi 5 has optical and coaxial inputs, sure, but that doesn't automatically equate to better sound.

DAC/amp combos don't necessarily have to come with major compromises, either. The $549 JDS Labs Element IV delivers up to 3.2 watts per channel into 32 ohms, and comes with features like automatic gain switching, EQ and even preamp outputs for powered speakers. That's more than enough for many demanding headphones, eliminating the need for a dedicated amplifier. The downside, of course, is that you're stuck with the combo and can't upgrade piecemeal.

While DAC/amp combos are great, a stack can still make sense for audiophiles who use a wide variety of headphones or who like to tinker with their hi-fi setup. Going with separates gives you the freedom to upgrade the amplifier down the line without giving up a perfectly capable DAC, or vice versa.

Certain headphones may also benefit from the power a dedicated amp can provide. Some high-impedance headphones just ask for a lot of power, while planar magnetic models, for example, can combine low impedance and low sensitivity. Let's take the HiFiMAN Susvara Unveiled, for example, which has a 45-ohm impedance and only 86 dB sensitivity. The Absolute Sound advises at least 6 watts of amplification, so a standalone amp may be the better choice here. However, too much power can be a bad thing, too: a very powerful amp may result in audible hiss with very sensitive headphones. So start by checking your headphones' power requirements and the amplifier's noise performance instead of just assuming that you need a beefy amp.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vorssaint is a powerful, modular utility suite, provided permissions are carefully managed.

macOS offers one of the most refined desktop experiences, but users looking for more granular control of their desktops might find the OS' native options limiting. Unlike Microsoft's PowerToys, which includes a collection of over 25 productivity and customization tools, Mac users must often turn to a fragmented selection of third-party applications to achieve similar levels of control. For example, macOS' native window tiling is serviceable at best, allowing for only a few tiling options regardless of screen size. Similarly, the OS doesn't natively support independent volume control and output device selection for individual applications. This is where Vorssaint, the Swiss Army Knife of macOS utility apps, comes into the picture.

Industry observers note that vorssaint is a third-party, open source application that aims to resolve macOS' productivity and customization pain points with a single menu-bar application. The app groups together a range of utility tools and nifty quick toggles to streamline productivity. The project is hosted on GitHub, and has earned over 33,000 stars and 230 contributors.

According to recent reports, vorssaint includes an impressive collection of utilities that aims to improve how people interact with their Macs. Its window-tiling feature offers more control over how users arrange their application windows, including edge snapping and shortcuts. The app also includes a toggle for clamshell mode, enabling MacBooks to continue running even with their lids closed, while its "Keep Awake" feature allows users to control when or if their Macs can enter a sleep state.

It has been revealed that the application suite also includes several handy tools that streamline daily workflows. For example, its screenshot utility supports scrolling screenshots, which makes it possible to capture content that extends beyond what's visible on the screen. People can also edit captured screenshots with the app's in-built image editing tool. Similarly, Vorssaint's media tool is capable of video compression, image conversion and text extraction from images. Meanwhile, its system monitoring tool extends beyond Mac's Activity Monitor, providing valuable information on thermals, memory usage and network speed.

Recent findings suggest that these are just a few examples of what Vorssaint offers. The suite also includes a graphical interface for Homebrew, URL cleaner and a powerful command bar. The command bar is akin to Apple's Spotlight search, but a lot more exciting. Its functionality extends beyond just searching apps and files; it can also be used to perform quick mathematical calculations, unit conversions and access most of Vorssaint's utilities by simply searching for them.

Recent findings suggest that vorssaint's robust utility stack undoubtedly makes it a promising productivity suite for power users. However, some of its powerful tools require sensitive macOS permissions. Depending on what features users install, the app may request permissions for Accessibility, Screen Recording, Full Disk Access and Automation. While granting these permissions is necessary to allow Vorssaint to perform some of its functions like taking screenshots, uninstalling applications and other system-level operations, users must understand what it means to grant system-level permissions to applications, especially those built by third-party developers.

According to recent reports, this is where Vorssaint's modular design becomes particularly useful, allowing owners to choose specific modules according to their requirements. For example, someone particularly interested in streamlining window management can choose to install only the Window layout module, and need not grant it screen recording and app management permissions. This selective approach lets users retain the modules they without having to risk granting sensitive permissions.

Industry News: How to clear your cache on Google TV

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (702 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you're experiencing slow performance or other issues with your Google TV, you may have heard about clearing the cache.
  • Recent findings suggest that even though Google TV manages app caches automatically, they can still get too large, especially if you have a lot of apps installed or store large video files on the TV or streaming box.
  • Sources indicate that thankfully, Android makes it easy to clear the cache, whether for individual apps or all installed apps, through its settings menu.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's worth trying if you're having issues.

If you're experiencing slow performance or other issues with your Google TV, you may have heard about clearing the cache. Caches generally help Android devices such as Google TVs run more smoothly by storing data — such as TV show thumbnails — that may need to be accessed rapidly later. While this may not be an issue on a device with plenty of storage, very few Google TV devices have more than the bare minimum there. The Google TV Streamer that replaced the Chromecast has 32GB of space, the bare minimum for an Android device, making cache management all the more crucial.

Recent findings suggest that even though Google TV manages app caches automatically, they can still get too large, especially if you have a lot of apps installed or store large video files on the TV or streaming box. App caches can also bloat or get corrupted, causing complications including slow performance, app crashes and frustrating system glitches.

Sources indicate that thankfully, Android makes it easy to clear the cache, whether for individual apps or all installed apps, through its settings menu. If your Google TV has become sluggish or glitchy over time, clearing the cache is a troubleshooting step you shouldn't skip.

Industry observers note that there are two ways to clear your Google TV cache: system-wide or per-app. If you're experiencing slowdowns or other challenges across the entire operating system, use the former option. The latter is best for when only a single app is giving you trouble.

To clear the cache system-wide, open Google TV settings by going to the home screen, holding down the home button on your remote or selecting your profile icon, and selecting the gear icon at the top of the quick settings panel. Go to System > Storage > Internal shared storage > Cached data, then select OK to clear the cached data for all of the apps on your device.

If only one app is acting up, clearing all the cache is overkill. Instead, go to Settings using the steps in the above paragraph, then select Apps > See all apps. Scroll to find and select the app you're having challenges with, then select Force Stop and confirm by selecting OK. Next, select Clear Cache and confirm by selecting OK. If you still have issues, it's worth clearing the cache system-wide using the above steps. If even that doesn't work, try rebooting the Google TV. Finally, if you still have trouble, go back to the app's settings page and clear both its cache and data. This will erase everything and return the app to its default state, so only use it as a last resort.

According to recent reports, while clearing the cache for all apps system-wide can make your Google TV device more responsive in the short term, it's a temporary fix for the real problem: insufficient storage. As noted earlier, Google TV devices rarely come with that much storage, and installing dozens of apps will rapidly eat through it.

In a recent development, it's generally good practice to keep approximately 10 percent of an Android device's storage empty. This buffer gives the system breathing room for operations that keep the drive healthy and to build robust app caches. If your Google TV storage is too full, clearing the cache likely won't resolve all your performance issues.

According to recent reports, after clearing the system-wide cache, go to Settings > System > Storage > Internal Shared Storage to see how much space your apps, movies, photos and other files are taking up. The remaining free space will be shown at the bottom. If 90 percent or more of the drive is full, it's time to start deleting things.

If media is the culprit, back the files up and delete them. For most Google TVs, though, the space-hogging culprit is likely installed apps. A good way to start is by deleting any apps you haven't used in a long time, especially if they're taking up an inordinate amount of space. Keeping that streaming service you downloaded to watch a single movie isn't worth the frustration of dealing with a slow TV.

You can personalize the SlideTag with a photo slideshow, message, or QR code transferred from your phone over Bluetooth.

Industry observers note that after expanding its Charmera collection with a Millennium Edition featuring Y2K-inspired designs earlier this year, Reto’s follow-up to its tiny Kodak camera is an equally small digital photo frame you can use to display your shots. But while the Charmera’s usefulness stopped at snapping grainy photos and terrible videos, the Kodak SlideTag goes one step further. It also functions as a Bluetooth tracker that’s compatible with either Apple’s Find My or Google’s Find Hub tracking networks.

The Kodak SlideTag will be available for $34.99 each and, like the Charmera, will feature a series of retro designs distributed in mystery boxes so you don’t know which one you’re going to get. Kodak also sells a complete set of all eight vintage designs for $279.92 if you don’t like mysteries; however, there’s a ninth “secret edition” only available in the individual boxes with a sleek metallic finish.

For those who grew up in an era where projectors are small enough to integrate into phones, the SlideTag is designed to look like a modernized version of the film slides that were used to project photos decades ago. Instead of film, the SlideTag features a 1.54-inch color E Ink screen that mixes six colored inks to display photos at a resolution of 240 x 240.

The color reproduction won’t be as accurate as an LCD or OLED screen, but the SlideTag can hold and cycle up to 12 photos transferred to the device over Bluetooth from Kodak’s Memory Link app running on a mobile device. You can also use it to display a short to-do list, contact details, a countdown timer, or a QR code linking to wherever you want.

As a tracker it’s not quite as functional as an Apple AirTag or Google’s Pixel Tag, which use features like ultra wideband (UWB) and Channel Sounding to make them easier to find. The SlideTag sticks to basic Bluetooth with a range of up to 30 meters out in the open and a 75-decibel buzzer to help locate it when you’re close. Battery life will vary depending on how frequently you use tracking features or refresh the displayed image, but the SlideTag uses a common CR2032 coin cell battery that’s easy to replace.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S.
  • According to recent reports, but investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future.
  • “We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history.

According to recent reports, but investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year.

“We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch.

Having navigated the complexities of U.S.-China relations firsthand, Notable was also convinced that “mission-critical” work would always require U.S.-based, closed-source models, Tung remarked.

In a recent development, less than two years later, Notable’s LPs are no longer questioning the outsized investment. On Wednesday, Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO in history, reaching a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion before its shares began trading the next day, a paper return of roughly 15 times.

Notable is, of course, not the only firm sitting on a massive paper windfall from Anthropic. Even traditional late-stage investors, who rarely see venture-scale multiples, are set for a big win.

Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC had been researching Anthropic throughout 2024, but it didn’t make its first investment until after Chris Emanuel, head of the fund’s tech investments, met with Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao at Che Fico, an Italian restaurant in San Francisco, in early 2025. Rao helped pique Emanuel’s interest in the tech giant by showing that model improvements were driving rising enterprise adoption. GIC then made its first investment in Anthropic’s Series F, a round announced in September 2025 at a $183 billion valuation.

Recent findings suggest that “Claude Code was just released then,” Emanuel told TechCrunch. “It was very early, but even then, we could see signs that it was really popular with developers.” GIC’s conviction in the AI lab was so high that the fund later led Anthropic’s Series G alongside Coatue at a $380 billion valuation, and returned as one of the co-leads for the pre-IPO round at $965 billion. Across the three rounds, GIC invested more than $4.5 billion in Anthropic, amassing a stake equal to about 1% of the company after its IPO, according to a person familiar with GIC’s financials.

Lilian Li, who leads U.S. growth investments at Baillie Gifford, began studying Anthropic and speaking with its team nearly two years before first investing in the company’s Series F. Baillie Gifford invested in the Claude maker once it became clear that the company was “executing consistently” on its vision while generating strong revenue and “compelling gross margins,” Li told TechCrunch.

After Baillie Gifford’s initial investment, Anthropic continued to deliver on its promises, expanding into industries such as legal services and life sciences, as well as broader applications like Cowork and cybersecurity, Li said.

According to recent reports, “It’s actually quite incredible how consistent they have been with how promptly everything’s been changing,” she added. Baillie Gifford went on to invest a total of $1.5 billion across three funding rounds, a bet that has generated substantial paper gains for the investment manager, as well as for dozens of other backers who invested at what once seemed like astronomical valuations.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Starlink's cheapest home proposal costs $44 less per month than it did in 2020, but hardware ownership and regional pricing have changed.
  • Starlink rolled out its public beta in October 2020, with the equipment costing $499 and the monthly subscription $99.
  • It has been revealed that the company also jacked up its residential rates in 2026, but the entry-level rate is still lower than it was in 2020.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Starlink's cheapest home proposal costs $44 less per month than it did in 2020, but hardware ownership and regional pricing have changed.

Starlink rolled out its public beta in October 2020, with the equipment costing $499 and the monthly subscription $99. Six years down the road, SpaceX's satellite internet service starts at $55 monthly for US customers, with equipment rentals available at no upfront cost in select areas. That's $44 less a month, or $528 less annually, on the subscription cost alone.

It has been revealed that the company also jacked up its residential rates in 2026, but the entry-level rate is still lower than it was in 2020. Throw in discounts and fluctuating rates based on local demand, and two customers could end up paying vastly different bills for the same satellite internet service.

SpaceX's first public beta was rolled out as the "Better Than Nothing Beta." True to its very transparent (and accurate) name, customers were asked to expect download speeds of 50 to 150 Mbps and latency of 20 to 40ms, paired with occasional periods of zero connectivity.

The hardware kit with the price tag of $499 included Starlink's original circular satellite dish, a mounting tripod and a Wi-Fi router. With the first $99 monthly subscription payment, the initial cost came to $598, excluding shipping and taxes. So if the monthly rate remained the same, the first year's total would've been $1,687, including the equipment.

What customers with reliable broadband might scoff at, though, could still be an acceptable price for those stuck with slow DSL or unreliable cellular service, even with occasional outages.

SpaceX did hike the monthly rates to $110 back in March 2022, and it took effect for current users in April 2022. The hardware cost also went up to $599 for new users and $549 for customers with existing deposits. The culprit, according to the firm, was inflation. In 2023, there were two prices for residential subscriptions: $90 in areas where there was excess network capacity and $120 in areas where there was limited network capacity.

The satellite internet service is now available with three primary residential aims: Residential 100 Mbps for $55 per month, Residential 200 Mbps for $85 and Residential Max at $130. Each plan offers unlimited data, but the first two are locked to speed limits. The Max plan does get higher network priority and claims speeds of 400 Mbps or higher in suitable conditions.

According to recent reports, starlink can be more expensive than cable, fiber or 5G home internet, but availability is where the value lies. The company's portable Roam service is available at $55 for 100GB of high-speed internet, after which speeds go down. If you don't want the high-speed data cap, Roam Unlimited costs $175 per month.

Latest Update: You can mass-delete all of your emails on Gmail in only a few clicks

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (689 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you have thousands of emails piling up in Gmail, this is for you.
  • In a recent development, you're more than welcome to delete your emails individually if you want to be there for a very long time.
  • In a recent development, in your computer browser (mobile browsers didn't make the cut), click on the Gear icon in the upper right corner to open Settings > See All Settings > Conversation View.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you have thousands of emails piling up in Gmail, this is for you.

In a recent development, you're more than welcome to delete your emails individually if you want to be there for a very long time. At two seconds per email, it would take a little over 11 hours of constant clicking to get through 20,000 emails — and honestly, 20,000 emails isn't much for a business Gmail account. Most people are familiar with methodically deleting 50 or even 100 emails at a time by checking the box in the top left and hitting the trash icon. But if you just want to wipe clean your entire inbox and start from scratch, you can do so on a browser.

In a recent development, in your computer browser (mobile browsers didn't make the cut), click on the Gear icon in the upper right corner to open Settings > See All Settings > Conversation View. Scroll down and tap Conversation View On. Now, go to your inbox. Check the box at the top of the message list to select all the current emails on the page. Once you check the box, a narrow banner should pop up at the top that gives you the option to select all (number of emails) conversations in Primary. Choose that option, take a deep breath, click the trash icon and confirm. Jump over to your Bin in the left column, select it and choose Empty Bin Now > Confirm.

If there's a particular thread you're concerned about, enter the name of the business, entity or person you want to find in the Ask Gmail search box at the top. The page will generate all conversations that have anything to do with the term you entered. Right-click one of those emails, select Find Emails From (insert search term), and skim the resulting page, archiving or otherwise protecting those emails from deletion.

There are a few tabs at the top of a default Gmail inbox, potentially with more categories depending on whether you've added some in the past. One of these tabs is labeled "Promotions," and these emails are probably the most aggravating besides Spam. Fortunately, you can mass-delete them in the same way. Click on Promotions > check the box at the top-left > Select all (number of Promotions emails) conversations in Promotions > Trash Icon > Confirm. You can rinse and repeat with every tab you want to wipe out.

According to recent reports, if you want to be a little more specific, you can also search. Type (category: promotions older_than: 1y) into the search bar to target all Promotions emails that are more than a year old. You can narrow it further by clicking on Showing most relevant and switching it to Showing most recent in the drop-down. Either way, Gmail's tools are fairly extensive, so you don't have to mass-delete every email in every tab, especially if you're worried about deleting something important. Once it's gone from the bin, it's gone for good.

Archive first and delete later. Archiving removes mail from your inbox, but the messages remain in All Mail and are searchable for future reference. Use the same select-all process; only click Archive instead of the trash icon. In the search bar, specify the emails you want to keep. For instance, type is: starred, is: notable or has: attachment. Toss some keywords in there if you're afraid of losing something more specific within those categories, like "offer" or "invoice." Using terms like "from: (email address)" will narrow it down to a specific email sender that you want to delete or keep.

According to recent reports, it's never a bad idea to at least skim through before you mass-delete everything you've received in your inbox over the last year or two. Using search terms makes it much easier, but it'll leave you a little cross-eyed if you stare at the screen long enough. Your best bet is to leave everything in the trash bin for a few days, just in case you remember an vital sender and you need to move it back to your inbox.

#2143. Industry News: Don't throw away your old Xbox — Do this instead

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1538 w)

Industry News: Don't throw away your old Xbox — Do this instead

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1538 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that letting old pieces of tech go is never easy, especially when you have fond memories of the original Xbox.
  • It has been revealed that make your Xbox One your go-to streaming box for the bedroom!
  • If we're talking Xbox One, you can download and enjoy many streaming services on Microsoft's last-gen console, including Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu and Paramount+.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that letting old pieces of tech go is never easy, especially when you have fond memories of the original Xbox. But no matter how much you loved shooting seven shades of alien goo out of the Covenant in Halo: Combat Evolved, it's unlikely you're still using a 25-year-old console on a daily basis. If you no longer touch your OG Xbox, Xbox 360 or Xbox One, as long as it's working, there are far better options than just tossing it out.

It has been revealed that make your Xbox One your go-to streaming box for the bedroom! Go retro — dust off that Xbox 360 and play those obscure DVD collections you've been hoarding for years! Many Xbox controllers can even be used to enjoy the best PC games! You could obviously make cash for your old console on auctioning sites like eBay. Or here's a thought: How about gifting your past-gen Xbox to a thrift store/charity shop? Your old Xbox deserves more respect than being dumped in a dustbin.

If we're talking Xbox One, you can download and enjoy many streaming services on Microsoft's last-gen console, including Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu and Paramount+. Skip back to Xbox 360 and sadly, you're mostly out of luck.

Provided you don't have a relative who is currently begging for your old console, why not keep it? These past-gen machines are still perfectly good bedroom streaming boxes, with the added bonus that you can still still play classics on them — like Aussie-set open-world racer Forza Horizon 3 — from the comfort of your sheets.

Recent findings suggest that xbox consoles have never been associated with watching physical media as much as their PlayStation counterparts. The PS2 was the DVD machine — the first console to embrace a media format that would comprehensively replace video tapes. Did the original Xbox also support DVDs? In a fiddly way... yes. You needed Microsoft's official Xbox DVD Movie Playback Kit, which came with an awkward dongle that needed to be plugged into a controller port to get it working. Not exactly an elegant solution.

In a recent development, if you're reading this, it's highly unlikely you're trying to repurpose the 25-year-old OG Xbox as a DVD player in an age of 4K Blu-ray players, but if you have kept either an Xbox 360 or Xbox One, those make a whole lot more sense as back-up media players. The 360 will happily play DVDs straight out of the box with zero tinkering required.

As for the Xbox One, it also plays DVDs and Blu-rays/4K Blu-rays, although the latter media type requires a free Blu-ray app download from the Microsoft Store. I used to occasionally watch UHD discs on my old Xbox One X, and the supercharged console provided perfectly decent UHD movie experiences with my 4K Blu-rays.

Industry observers note that microsoft has done a tremendous job with backwards-compatibility for several generations. Skip back to Xbox One X, and the company offered free 4K upgrades for select original Xbox games and 360 titles. These gratis updates include some absolute bangers, like Crackdown, Conker: Live & Reloaded, Halo: Reach, Red Dead Redemption, Mirror's Edge, and many more (well, provided you still own the game).

In total, 13 OG Xbox games got Xbox One X Enhanced features, while 21 Xbox 360 titles received similar big time resolution boosts thanks to the supercharged console's 6 TFLOPS. For context, the Xbox Series X can tap into 12.15 TFLOPS of GPU power.

Industry observers note that the Xbox One X, Xbox One and Xbox One S will all play an impressive 632 Xbox 360 games! Microsoft's backward compatibility program deserves all the flowers. Though sadly, Xbox has mostly dropped its commitment to adding new original Xbox and 360 titles to Game Pass since late 2021.

The Xbox 360 remains an excellent console for retro fans. Though you'll need a hard drive so that the console can store emulation profiles, around 480 original Xbox games can be enjoyed on the 360. That's pretty impressive considering Microsoft's colossal black box released just shy of 1,000 titles over the course of its life. Sony's commitment to backwards-combability has rarely impressed on the other hand, but you still shouldn't throw away an old PlayStation either.

Let's be honest. There's no way you're actually taking the title of this article literally. If you are legitimately thinking about disposing of your old Xbox like it was yesterday's milk, please recycle it in a safe and eco-safe manner instead. Before you needlessly boot away your console, consider gifting it to someone else. Think of all those who could benefit from an aging Xbox. Young relatives! Charities! Children's hospitals! Your Xbox donation could genuinely make a kid's Christmas.

Recent findings suggest that of course, if you could use the extra money, the Xbox One X still goes for upwards of $150 on eBay. Reputable buy-back sites like Back Market Trade-in will give you cash for your console. The site currently accepts pretty much every Xbox in existence (though broken units obviously won't fetch you much). If your Xbox One X is in flawless condition and comes with a controller and 1GB of storage, you can currently net a pretty tasty $185.

Sadly, Back Market isn't the place to sell an old Xbox 360. At time of writing, even if it's in great condition and comes with a controller, the site will only pony up a pathetic $3 for the classic console. Your best chance of raking in some folding money for that old 360 is by selling it on auction sites like eBay and Swappa.

Unless we're talking about the OG Xbox "Duke" controller, gamepads since the Xbox 360 generation can generally be repurposed to work on gaming PCs. The wired Xbox 360 controller should work just fine with a Windows 11 PC as long as you plug it into one of your rig's USB ports  — Steam is still very good at recognizing old school gamepad layouts, especially in Big Picture Mode. With non-wireless 360 controllers, you'll likely need a cheap Microsoft wireless receiver.

It has been revealed that there is a chance the Major Boy OG 2001 Xbox controller can function with a Series machine, yet it demands precision work. Getting the 2001 Duke to play nice with an Xbox Series X or S requires a special adapter and third-party software. Compared to this hassle, a Xbox 360 pad should still get along with most modern, Steam-compliant PCs without much issue. Well, as long as you've taken care of mentioned peripheral over the years.

It has been revealed that xbox One controllers obviously work on Xbox Series X/S consoles, so it's unlikely you're going to throw them aside just because they lack a dedicated Share button. You can pair a Xbox One gamepad to a PC either through a USB cable, Bluetooth connection or picking up the Xbox Wireless Adapter for a hand-free wireless experience that's more reliable than BT.

According to recent reports, if you've finally decided to sell your old Xbox, then you might want to back up your old saves. More importantly, to protect your privacy/delete credit cards you might have stored on the console, you must factory reset your system before selling it.

According to recent reports, provided your Xbox One is connected to the interwebs, backing up saves is an idiot-proof process before the big step of a factory reset. Your console automatically backs up game saves every time you sign into your console. To secure old saves for the last time before selling your Xbox One, make sure it's online and sign into your usual account. Then it's a case of briefly opening any game you want to keep data from, let your console's "Syncing data" message finish, save and quit out of the game, and you're good to go. If you then decide to buy an Xbox Series X or S, you can download this data from the cloud.

Now it's time to factory reset your Xbox One. Navigate to Profile & system > Settings > System > Console info > Reset console. Choose Reset and remove everything (which deletes all apps, games and local saves). Your Xbox One will be wiped clean.

If you're keen on keeping old Xbox 360 saves, plug an empty USB drive into the console, then go to Settings > System > Storage > and choose Configure Now. The 360 will format the drive in its proprietary FAT32 system, at which you can go back to Storage > Hard Drive > Games and Apps. From here, simply select the games whose data you want to preserve, then click Copy > USB Storage Device.

To factory reset your Xbox 360, head to Settings > System > Storage, select your hard drive, press Y for Device Options, then select Format. If the console asks you for the serial number at this point, you can find it from System > Console Settings > System Info and note it down. Once your 360 has been formatted, it's ready to sell.

With all of these steps complete, your old Xbox is now good to move on to its next owner.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Your Ring doorbell can work in tandem with lots of other smart devices.
  • It has been revealed that your Ring doorbell can be so much more than just a doorbell.
  • The Ring's compatibility with so many smart home devices can make your life much more convenient by simply pairing them and controlling them all through the Ring app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your Ring doorbell can work in tandem with lots of other smart devices.

It has been revealed that your Ring doorbell can be so much more than just a doorbell. Of course you're familiar with its helpful functions, like high-resolution video up to 4K, Live View, Two-way Talk, 3D Motion Detection and night vision. What you may not know is that your Ring doorbell can seamlessly connect to all kinds of other smart home gadgets.

The Ring's compatibility with so many smart home devices can make your life much more convenient by simply pairing them and controlling them all through the Ring app.

Why limit your view to just your porch when you can pair wired and wireless cameras throughout your entire property? Ring alone offers more than two dozen security camera options to pair with your doorbell, including indoor and outdoor spotlight and floodlight cameras. If you're looking to pair a camera not made by Ring, you can do so through the Ring Alarm Pro Base Station and Ring ONVIF support. This enables your Ring system to pair with dozens of other brands, as long as their cameras are ONVIF-compatible.

In a recent development, besides cameras, your Ring doorbell is directly compatible with Ring panic buttons, window and door sensors, glass break sensors, sump pump monitors, smoke and carbon monoxide listeners, and air-quality monitors — all controllable through the Ring app — for even more peace of mind. It's vital to note, however, that some of these sensors and accessories may require the Ring Alarm Base Station hub to connect directly with the Ring app. It's a good idea to check your Ring app to find out which accessories are directly compatible.

You can also connect certain smart locks directly through the Ring app without needing the Ring Alarm Base Station. If you already have the Ring Alarm Base Station, however, your options increase quite a bit as more manufacturers make smart locks that can be connected to your Ring through the base station via Z-Wave radio frequencies. These locks allow you to lock and unlock your door through the Ring app, a PIN or your key.

Through the Ring app, you can set up a wide range of lighting options, like outdoor spotlights, steplights, floodlights, wall lights and path lights... even some that are solar-powered. By adding outdoor lighting options, you not only improve your Ring doorbell's camera performance with extra light, but you can also create customized lighting zones, turn lights on and off when you're not home, and program the lights to illuminate when motion is detected.

According to recent reports, if your home is already equipped with landscape lighting, you can still connect it to your Ring system through the Ring transformer so you can control it through the Ring app. Third-party wireless smart bulbs and other lighting accessories, however, can't be directly connected through the Ring app. But there are workarounds. For example, with the Ring outdoor smart plug, you can turn any "dumb" lights (like most holiday lighting and inflatables) into smart ones by simply plugging them into the smart plug and controlling them with the Ring app.

In a recent development, taking advantage of your Ring doorbell isn't limited to outdoor devices. For example, if you own a compatible smart thermostat, you can connect it to your Ring app and control your home's climate right from the Ring dashboard in your app.

And if you want a better look at what's going on outside your home, there's no better way than on a big-screen smart TV. Through an Amazon Fire TV or Fire TV Stick and the Alexa app, all it takes is a simple voice command through your Alexa remote to show you the front door. Fire TV systems even support picture-in-picture, which pops onto your screen as soon as your doorbell button is pushed. But Ring viewing is also available with newer Samsung Smart TVs through Samsung's SmartThings smart home platform. While the experience isn't quite as smooth as with Fire TVs, the SmartThings app does let you connect your Ring doorbell and manually open the camera to view it on the SmartThings dashboard on your TV.

A very useful — and underappreciated — device you can pair with your Ring doorbell is a smart water valve, which allows you to remotely shut off your water supply in the event of a leak to prevent potentially disastrous flooding. Installation requires plumbing the smart water valve into the main water line and then setting up the valve through the Moen Smart Water app. Ring also integrates with some third-party Z-Wave smart water valves.

Industry observers note that yes, you can even bring Ring technology into your vehicle with the Ring Car Cam and the Ring Car Tracker and Alarm. The dual-facing Car Cam mounts onto your dashboard and keeps an eye on your surroundings, whether the car is parked or in motion. The Car Tracker and Alarm plugs right into your vehicle's OBD-II port and sends push notifications if there are disturbances, including physical impact, a door that's been forced open or towing. This device also offers GPS tracking of your car on your Ring dashboard. Both car accessories are easily integrated into the Ring app so you can keep tabs on everything right on your phone.

You may already have a smart garage door opener for your home, but pairing it with your Ring doorbell makes life just a little bit easier. Compatible several major garage door opener brands, the Ring app essentially serves as a shortcut for your garage door, so you have quick access to check on your home.

It has been revealed that by integrating the apps, you can instantly check the status of your garage door on the Ring app dashboard as you view your doorbell and/or camera feeds. This also lets you control your garage door right from your Ring screen, so you can open and close it without using your garage door app. A nice bonus is that this app integration also delivers access to Amazon Key in-garage delivery, which provides Amazon drivers with access to your garage door and allows them to slip your packages securely into your garage before closing the door.

Recent findings suggest that you've probably noticed that Ring doorbells are easily paired with Amazon services and devices. That's because Amazon owns Ring, so that effortless integration is intentional by design. And it's quite convenient if you own an Echo Show, Echo Dot or Fire TV. By syncing your Ring doorbell with your Alexa-controlled Amazon device, you can easily set up announcements whenever someone is at your front door, instantly view the live stream of your camera by simply asking Alexa to show you the front door and even communicate with whoever is at your front door through any Alexa speaker... all without ever having to look at your phone.

The Alexa integration is also beneficial if you want to connect third-party devices and gadgets that aren't directly compatible with your Ring doorbell. These include smart lights and bulbs, smart plugs and switches, thermostats, locks, and TVs. All you need is the Alexa app to set it all up and view it in your Ring app.

#2141. Tech Report: The drawbacks of adding solar panels to your home

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1075 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: The drawbacks of adding solar panels to your home

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1075 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the surface, adding solar panels to your home seems like a fantastic idea.
  • With all that in mind, why wouldn't you want to add solar panels to your home?
  • The average price to install a solar power system in a typical home falls between $20,000 and $27,000, with a national benchmark of $3.36 per watt, before any incentives or rebates are applied.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the surface, adding solar panels to your home seems like a fantastic idea. They can cut down your monthly electricity bills, potentially increase the resale value of your home and deliver clean, renewable and environmentally friendly energy to your residence. Some states and utility companies even provide solar incentives to homeowners in the form of rebates and income tax credits.

With all that in mind, why wouldn't you want to add solar panels to your home? Well, for all the good they can do, solar panels also come with plenty of drawbacks, especially if you don't live in a state with solar-friendly regulations, your home isn't geographically positioned to take full advantage of solar energy or your electricity bill isn't all that high to begin with.

The average price to install a solar power system in a typical home falls between $20,000 and $27,000, with a national benchmark of $3.36 per watt, before any incentives or rebates are applied. Prior to 2026, homeowners could rely on a federal 30 percent tax credit to soften the blow, but the Trump administration terminated that incentive.

According to recent reports, the upfront expense might not be worth the investment, depending on a few factors. First, consider your electricity rate and usage. Some areas charge more for electricity than others, with the 10 most expensive states being Hawaii, Maine, Massachusetts, California, Alaska, Upcoming York, Rhode Island, New Hampshire, New Jersey and Connecticut.

If you don't reside in one of those states, installing solar power may not significantly impact your electricity bill, especially if you live in a smaller home, have a small household (people-wise), use energy-efficient appliances and tend not to consume much energy in a given month.

You should also research whether your utility tech giant offers net metering or other incentives and rebates. Net metering gives homeowners credits for any excess energy produced by their solar panels, allowing you to reduce or even potentially erase a monthly electric bill. This incentive is not available everywhere, and the programs differ by state.

According to recent reports, for example, the most advantageous programs for solar panel users offer a one-to-one power exchange that credits you at the same retail rate you pay for your power. Other states utilize buyback programs or reduced-rate or net billing structures that credit homeowners a portion of what they pay for energy.

According to recent reports, some geographic locations are simply better than others when it comes to solar panels. Places with consistent sunlight and moderate-to-cool temperatures are best. An abundance of overcast weather or excessive heat can negatively impact panel performance and life.

Industry observers note that the design of your house also needs to be considered. Solar panels are almost always installed on roofs that face south and are clear of buildings, trees or other objects that may block sunlight. If your roof is on the older side, solar panels aren't ideal unless you have a new roof installed, and that can cost anywhere from $4,000 to more than $35,000 depending on the size of your home and the type of roof.

In a recent development, then there are simple aesthetics. Some homeowners, especially those who just paid for a brand new roof, don't want to cover it up with bulky and — let's face it — unattractive solar panels. Solar shingles are an alternative option, but they've attracted some negative press and also cost roughly twice the price per watt as standard solar panels. At $21 to $25 per square foot installed, the price to install solar shingles on a 2,500-square-foot home comes to between $52,500 and $62,500 before incentives.

Aside from lowering monthly electric bills and moving toward clean energy, having backup power during blackouts is a major appeal for homeowners looking to switch to solar, but it's not as simple as many people think. When your home loses power, solar energy doesn't just kick into gear. It requires a battery backup system that stores excess solar energy from the panels, then delivers it to your home when the power is out. And — you guessed it — it's expensive.

It has been revealed that for a single-battery backup system, which is enough to power the average home's lights, refrigerator, WiFi and some power outlets during outages, you're looking at spending between $10,000 and $16,000. If you want a whole-home, multi-battery backup, which can power your home's HVAC system and all appliances, that price range escalates to $22,000 to $40,000, plus routine maintenance costs.

That all combines to drastically increase your solar investment and potentially extend the payback period, which can lead to major problems if you decide you want to move before the system is paid off.

Solar panels can add resale value to your home, but there's a major caveat to consider: If you haven't fully paid off the cost of your home's solar equipment, prospective homebuyers may view that as a negative.

It has been revealed that why? Because if you opted to finance the installation cost or entered into a power purchase agreement (PPA) with your utility firm, the buyer must agree to assume the remainder of the contract. If the buyer refuses to take over the contract, the most straightforward solution is to pay off the balance. Unfortunately, that's also the most expensive solution.

Here's another drawback: whoever buys your home must also qualify for the lease on the solar equipment. Being approved for a mortgage is separate from being approved for a solar lease, so if the buyer isn't approved for the solar lease, the entire home sale could fall apart. Plus, the lease-approval process can take up to two months, so this would need to be taken care of well ahead of closing.

Then there's the UCC-1, which is essentially a lien against the solar equipment filed by most solar leasing companies with local land registries. Because the UCC-1 turns up in property title searches, this can turn into a huge problem if the buyer's mortgage lender refuses to close the transaction because of this open, pending issue. And it does happen because the bank providing the mortgage loan does not want to have a solar company standing in front of them should the house need to be seized and sold by the lender to recoup its money. Lenders can, and do, often refuse to provide the buyer with the loan as long as the UCC-1 remains active.

#2140. Breaking: What the little clock icon at the top of your Samsung phone means

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (771 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: What the little clock icon at the top of your Samsung phone means

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (771 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three different icons can pass for a clock on your Galaxy phone, and each one has an easy fix.
  • You're fiddling on your phone and that bar at the top of your screen is peppered with various icons.
  • There are tons of icons that can show up in your Android status bar, so what exactly does that clock represent?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three different icons can pass for a clock on your Galaxy phone, and each one has an easy fix.

You're fiddling on your phone and that bar at the top of your screen is peppered with various icons. There's your battery level, the Wi-Fi icon, the signal bars — but what's that tiny clock doing there?

There are tons of icons that can show up in your Android status bar, so what exactly does that clock represent? Is there something wrong with your phone? Well, the good news is that it's rarely a cause for concern, unless you're terrified of waking up bright and early (which we get). Depending on the exact shape, the clock icon usually points to one of a few straightforward explanations, each with an easy fix. There's a good chance that the icon shows you have an active alarm set up.

Let's dive deeper into what the clock icon means, how to get rid of it and which other symbols might be causing similar confusion on your Galaxy device.

In a recent development, the most likely reason you're seeing a clock icon on your screen is that you set an alarm on your phone. Specifically, you've done this through Samsung's Clock app and not some other tool. You'll find the clock right next to the Wi-Fi signal when the entire Quick Settings panel is expanded.

When the alarm is 30, 15 or five minutes away from ringing, as per the clock settings, the clock icon becomes visible whenever you check your phone, moving to the left of the screen next to the time. In my testing, however, it also popped up at the 20- and 10-minute markers. When you swipe down the notifications panel, you'll even notice a message asking if you want to turn off the upcoming alarm. If you dismiss the notification, the clock icon only remains visible next to the Wi-Fi signal, going back to the original view. The icon shows up again as the alarm time approaches.

The only way to make the clock icon go away completely is to disable any active alarms. You'll have to go to the Clock app on your Samsung phone, tap the Alarm tab at the bottom and toggle off or delete any alarms you have set up. Once that's done, the icon immediately vanishes from the status bar.

Sources indicate that not every clock-shaped icon is an alarm you forgot you set up, however. If you see a rounded square with a small clock inside, it means your phone has a newly introduced software update available. You've probably had your phone pester you about that update and you've ignored it time and time again, so now it's a simple symbol in your status bar. The only way to dismiss this one once and for all is to actually install that update — sorry to break it to you, but you'll have to let the phone do its thing for a few minutes.

According to recent reports, go to Settings and scroll down to Software update. Select Check for updates to install the latest version of One UI. One UI 9 is at the moment rolling out to more and more Samsung Galaxy phones, so you're likely due for that update anyway. For some older phones, One UI 9 is the final major update.

According to recent reports, these two are not the only clock-looking symbols you can find in the bar on a Samsung phone. There's another one that gets mistaken for a clock: the Light performance profile indicator. This one is found exclusively on newer Samsung flagship models, such as the Galaxy Z Flip 4 and later, Galaxy Z Fold 4 and later, and Galaxy S23 and later models. This icon looks more like a speedometer than a clock and also features a small white leaf.

According to recent reports, the Light performance mode is designed to reduce power consumption. It will do this by lowering the phone's processing speed, which in turn helps extend battery life. It's a great tool to use when you're scrolling through social media or watching videos. If you start a game, the mode is automatically disabled so you can enjoy all that your phone can actually do.

If you don't know how the Light performance mode got turned on, you probably touched the icon in the Quick Settings panel by mistake. Just swipe down from the top of the screen and look for the tile and tap it again. Whatever icon you were looking at, you should now know how to get rid of it.

5 Apple Watch settings that can help you save its battery life

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1408 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A few changes can help give your Apple Watch extra hours of battery when you need it all day.
  • Among the improvements the Apple Watch receives with each iteration, battery life is something everyone wants more of.
  • If your Apple Watch's battery health has depleted significantly, bringing it in for a battery replacement could help restore its original endurance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A few changes can help give your Apple Watch extra hours of battery when you need it all day.

Among the improvements the Apple Watch receives with each iteration, battery life is something everyone wants more of. The company touts that the Apple Watch Series 12 lasts for 24 hours on a full charge. Apple measures this using a combination of 300 time checks, 15 minutes of app use, six hours of sleep tracking, 90 notifications and a 60-minute workout alongside music playback. Real-world results will naturally vary depending on how much you use your Apple Watch every day.

If your Apple Watch's battery health has depleted significantly, bringing it in for a battery replacement could help restore its original endurance. You can check battery health status on your watch by navigating to Settings > Battery > Battery Health. Power users might want to look at the Apple Watch Ultra 4 as their next buy since it's better equipped to handle constant, demanding usage with its larger battery.

That remarked, there are a handful of software tricks you can use to squeeze more battery life out of your existing Apple Watch, especially if it's not yet due for a battery replacement. Some of these are simple toggles to enable, while others involve making small adjustments to how you use your watch throughout the day.

The easiest way to extend your Apple Watch's battery life when it's running low is to turn on Low Power Mode. You can access this feature by pressing the side button, tapping the battery percentage and selecting Low Power Mode.

It has been revealed that an information card will display the first time you use this feature — scroll down and tap on Turn On. Alternatively, you can choose to keep Low Power Mode on for one, two or three days if you know you'll be away from a charger for a while. You can also access this battery saver feature by heading to Settings > Battery.

A few changes are immediately noticeable when you turn Low Power Mode on. The Always On display is disabled, as are the Wrist Flick and Double Tap gestures. Your watch will still light up its display automatically when you raise your wrist. Background heart rate and blood oxygen measurements are also paused; you can use their respective apps to get manual readings at any time, but low, high or irregular heart rate notifications are disabled. Losing basic health tracking features can be a dealbreaker to many.

Industry observers note that apple notes that Siri requests can take longer on the Apple Watch when it's in Low Power Mode, too. Live Activities and the complications on your watch face will patch less frequently and scrolling may stutter a bit. Your Apple Watch will continue to receive notifications and calls, but only if its paired iPhone is nearby. When you launch an app that requires internet access, Low Power Mode temporarily turns on Wi-Fi or cellular data.

Recent findings suggest that the Apple Watch works best when it's near its paired iPhone, but it can also connect to the internet on its own when needed. Any Apple Watch can connect to Wi-Fi networks, while cellular models offer even greater freedom by utilizing mobile data.

However, Apple recommends keeping the two devices nearby when you need to maximize battery life on your watch. This is because the Apple Watch piggybacks on its paired iPhone's internet connection over Bluetooth. When your devices are connected, you'll spot a tiny green phone icon in Control Center on your Apple Watch.

Recent findings suggest that cellular connectivity is convenient, but if you're somewhere that has Wi-Fi available, using that instead can conserve battery life. When you're not actively using your watch and don't mind it being disconnected for a while, you can stretch its endurance even further by enabling Airplane Mode. Find all these toggles in Control Center or access them through the Settings app.

Even without access to an internet connection, your Apple Watch can track workouts, play music or podcasts that have been downloaded, make purchases using Apple Pay and track your sleep. A good chunk of the built-in apps, like Alarms, Timers, Medications and Voice Memos, also work just fine.

It has been revealed that the Apple Watch is much more than just a fitness tracker. It can come in handy when your iPhone isn't nearby and you receive a call or message. Newer models come with improved speakers capable of playing music directly. And when you install an app on your iPhone, your Apple Watch will automatically install its companion version (if available).

According to recent reports, this is all great for convenience, but means your watch might end up with a bunch of apps you don't really need on your wrist. Those apps might also increase battery consumption by refreshing in the background and sending you notifications. Using the built-in speakers consumes more battery than connecting headphones does.

Start by uninstalling unneeded apps from your watch directly, which doesn't remove them from your iPhone. If you use an app on your Apple Watch occasionally but don't need it constantly fetching fresh information, navigate to Settings > General > Background App Refresh and turn its toggle off. It's also an option to disable Background App Refresh entirely, but this will affect all apps on your watch.

Sources indicate that you can also disable certain app notifications if you don't want your watch constantly buzzing on your wrist. By default, app notifications you've disabled on your iPhone will also be disabled on your Apple Watch, but you can customize which apps send notifications to your watch independently through the Watch app on your iPhone.

In a recent development, navigate to Notifications, scroll down to the Mirror iPhone Alerts From section and disable the toggles for any apps you don't want sending notifications to your Apple Watch. Fewer notifications mean fewer vibrations, fewer screen wake-ups and thus potentially less battery drain throughout the day.

Industry observers note that for a more granular approach, you're able to turn off Always On display without giving up the other features Low Power Mode shuts off. On your Apple Watch, navigate to Settings > Display & Brightness > Always On and turn the toggle off.

Alternatively, this menu has options to customize what information reveals on the Always On display, such as Live Activities or complication data. Macworld tested how big of a difference turning this feature off makes, and reported that disabling Always On display extended battery life on the Apple Watch by an impressive 10 to 12 hours.

To minimize screen-on time, always cover your watch with your palm when you're done using it. You might also want to turn off the Wake on Wrist Raise toggle (in the same menu) to prevent your watch from lighting up accidentally. Since Low Power Mode disables other gestures, it's fair to assume that shutting off features like Double Tap and Wrist Flick could help conserve a little more battery. You can find these toggles by navigating to Settings > Gestures.

It has been revealed that if you don't like the barebones feel of the Apple Watch when using Low Power Mode, you can configure it to only kick in during specific workouts. This is a great option if you regularly track longer exercise sessions and are willing to sacrifice some workout tracking features in exchange for longer battery life. In watchOS 27, the Workout app introduced two new options that turn Low Power Mode on during workouts.

According to recent reports, open the Workout app, select an activity type and tap the Goals and Targets button in the top-right corner. Scroll down and tap on Extended, then select Extended Workout to start tracking your activity. Some workouts have a second Max Extended Workout option as well that reduces the frequency of GPS and heart rate measurements. It will also disable alerts, splits and certain metrics like current pace during the workout. Once you finish the exercise, Low Power Mode will automatically turn off.

If you want the battery saver feature to kick in automatically every time you start a workout, navigate to Settings > Workout and turn the Low Power Mode toggle on. This eliminates the need for you to manually select the Extended Workout option each time — it's one of those underrated Apple Watch features that are easy to miss.

#2138. Here's when a Raspberry Pi 5 could be considered overkill

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (810 w)
